items.prompt: A DEPLOYER on the owning team sends POST /api/deployments for that app's production environment. What comes back?
items.answer: 403 with "Role DEPLOYER cannot deploy to production"
distractors: 201 Created, as DEPLOYER is listed for the deploy action
423 Locked, because production is always deploy-locked
400 Invalid payload, since the schema refuses that slug
items.explanation: canPerform(DEPLOYER, "deploy") passes, but ENV_DEPLOY_PERMISSIONS.DEPLOYER is ["dev", "staging"], so canDeployToEnvironment fails and the handler returns 403 with that message. Nothing in the schema checks slugs, and 423 needs deployLocked or deployFrozen.

items.prompt: A request sends x-user-email: nobody@example.com and no user has that email. Who does getActor return?
items.answer: The oldest user, from findFirst ordered by createdAt
distractors: null, so every later role check sees no actor at all
The owner@acme.dev user, the default for a missing header
A new user row, created on the fly for that email
items.explanation: findUnique misses, so getActor falls through to prisma.user.findFirst({ orderBy: { createdAt: "asc" } }). The owner@acme.dev default only applies when the header is empty, and nothing creates users.

items.prompt: At this commit, POST /api/deployments pairs app A's applicationId with app B's environmentId. What happens?
items.answer: Roles are checked on B's team, then the row is written under A
distractors: 404 Environment not found: the lookup matches both ids
Roles are checked on A's team, then the write is refused
400 Invalid payload, since Zod checks that the pair matches
items.explanation: The environment is loaded by id alone (route.js:48-55), so getTeamRole uses environment.application.teamId (app B), and createDeployment receives parsed.data with app A's applicationId. The guide records this as a known gap.

items.prompt: maskedSecret is called with an 8-character secret. How many of its characters stay visible?
items.answer: Four, the first two and the last two
distractors: Two, only the first two characters
None, as short values become all stars
Six, every character but the middle two
items.explanation: An 8-character value is not shorter than 6, so maskedSecret keeps slice(0, 2), adds value.length - 4 = 4 stars, and keeps slice(-2). Only values under 6 characters become all stars.
compareVersions compares numeric parts, so the sorted latest is v1.10.0 and the patch goes up by one. "v1.3.5" is what a plain string sort would give.

items.prompt: transitionDeployment is asked to move a LIVE deployment to DEPLOYING. What happens?
distractors: It updates the status and resets completedAt back to null
It writes the audit entry first, then rejects the change
It succeeds, as LIVE may return to any earlier status
items.explanation: DEPLOYMENT_TRANSITIONS.LIVE is ["ROLLED_BACK"], so canTransitionStatus fails and the function throws before prisma.deployment.update or writeAuditEntry run.

items.prompt: What does rollbackDeployment do to the deployment it rolls back?
items.answer: Nothing; a new ROLLED_BACK row points at it via rollbackOfId
distractors: It moves that row to ROLLED_BACK through transitionDeployment
It deletes that row and restores the previous LIVE deployment
It marks that row FAILED, then stamps its completedAt time
items.explanation: rollbackDeployment only reads the original and calls prisma.deployment.create with status "ROLLED_BACK" and rollbackOfId: deploymentId. The original row is never updated, which keeps history immutable.

items.prompt: Compared with POST /api/deployments, which check does POST /api/cli/deploy leave out?
items.answer: Every role check: no getTeamRole and no canPerform call
distractors: Zod parsing: the raw JSON goes straight to createDeployment
The env lookup: it trusts an environmentId from the body
Versioning: each CLI deploy is written as v1.0.0 again
items.explanation: The CLI route still safeParses the body, finds the environment by applicationId + slug and lets createDeployment pick the next version, but it never resolves a role, so anyone who can reach it can deploy.

items.prompt: PATCH /api/feature-flags sets enabled: true on a flag whose dependency flag is still disabled. What is the response?
items.answer: 409, with "Dependency not enabled:" and the blocking flag's key
distractors: 403, because enabling a dependent flag needs the OWNER role
200, and the dependency is switched on along with the flag
423 Locked, until the dependency's kill switch is cleared
items.explanation: When parsed.data.enabled === true the handler looks for a dependency whose dependsOnFlag is not enabled and returns 409 naming its key. editFlags allows OWNER and DEPLOYER, and nothing enables the dependency for you.

items.prompt: What string does encryptSecret store for a value?
items.answer: Three hex parts joined by colons: iv, auth tag, ciphertext
distractors: Base64 ciphertext with a sha256 of the key prefixed for lookup
Two hex parts, iv and ciphertext; GCM keeps no separate tag
The ciphertext alone, since the iv is derived from the key
items.explanation: It returns `${iv}:${tag}:${encrypted}` in hex. The iv is randomBytes(12) per call and decryptSecret needs the tag for setAuthTag.

items.prompt: Why does lib/prisma.js keep the client on globalThis outside production?
items.answer: So dev hot reloads reuse one client rather than open new pools
distractors: So components marked "use client" can import the database directly
So every production server instance shares a single connection
So Prisma logs only errors and stays quiet during development
items.explanation: The global is set only when NODE_ENV !== "production"; it stops each hot reload from building another PrismaClient. Client components never import it, and in development the client logs warn and error.

items.prompt: In the Zustand store, what does setSelectedEnvironmentId(id) do to the other two selections?
items.answer: selectedAppId is kept; selectedDeploymentId becomes null
distractors: Both are reset to null, the same as when setSelectedAppId runs
Both are kept; only selectedEnvironmentId changes in the store
selectedAppId is reset and selectedDeploymentId is kept as-is
items.explanation: set merges shallowly: the returned object holds selectedEnvironmentId and selectedDeploymentId: null, so selectedAppId is untouched. Only setSelectedAppId resets both children.

items.back: BUILDING -> DEPLOYING or FAILED; DEPLOYING -> LIVE or FAILED; LIVE -> ROLLED_BACK; FAILED -> ROLLED_BACK; ROLLED_BACK is terminal. Unknown statuses allow nothing.

items.front: Which environments can each role deploy to, and which actions need OWNER?
items.back: OWNER: dev, staging, production. DEPLOYER: dev, staging. VIEWER: none. Only OWNER may lockDeploys; deploy, rollback, editSecrets and editFlags allow OWNER and DEPLOYER. Unknown roles or actions get an empty list.

items.front: Zustand vs TanStack Query in this app
items.back: Zustand (lib/store.js) holds UI state only: selected app, environment, deployment and log filters. TanStack Query holds server state from /api/bootstrap; every mutation invalidates ["bootstrap"] to refetch it.

items.front: The two known gaps in POST /api/deployments at this commit
items.back: 1) The environment is looked up by id only, so app A's applicationId can be paired with app B's environment (roles and freeze checked on B, row written under A). 2) An unknown x-user-email falls back to the oldest user.
